asr.full_text: Hello everyone, I hope you are well! So today we will take a video about the Sleepage. If you have already used PancakeSwap, or on other applications, you have probably already heard about the sleepage. When you want to buy Cryptos, say SafeMoon for example, It tells you to set the sleepage, that is the tolerance of the sleepage at 12%. I'm pretty sure you have already done this operation, You can change the tolerance of the slippage to 12% so you may have already executed this operation change the tolerance of the slippage you may make it vary what does it mean? the slippage is the difference between the price at which you want to cross your order and the price of the market you want to pay when your order is executed the tolerance of the slippage we tolerate a small gap between the price we pass our order and the final price when it will be executed on the market when we put a tolerance of slippage of 12% we are ready to pay 12% more or if we are a seller we are ready to sell 12% below the price that we had decided. Why is there slippage? The slippage can appear for different reasons on the market as there is a very volatile market like in any other crypto it is between the moment of your order and when it is executed on the market the price can vary dramatically so that's why often these coins have a sleep age rate we have a rather high tolerance of sleep that to be fair as the price remains stable it is not the case that all is to say that you may spend more sleepage if not it has much effect that can in some places also be a very good thing that's why often these pieces we have a higher slippage tolerance, to stand out from any volatility. so the second reason might be due to the size of your order so if the buying and selling price are in a disbalance for example you want to buy a certain quantity of pieces at a defined price but there isn't enough of each seller with each the seller has not enough of a piece to meet your demand you will have to find other sellers who may sell at a higher price so here too it will be important to have a tolerance on the sleep edge I'll give an example illustrated so you understand better For example I want to buy 10 croissants so in my city there are three bakeries the first bakeries they sell the crescent at 1 euro, the second bakery they sell the croissant 2 euros and the third bakeries they The first bakery sells croissants for 1 euro, the second bakery sells croissants for € 2 and the third bakery sells croissants for € 3. So I would like to buy 10 croissants. I want to buy them in the first bakery, I would like to spend an amount of 10 euros to buy ten croissants, except that the first bakery only has 7 croissants left. So what do I do? I will already buy these 7 croissants here and I will go to the second bakery. And here at the second bakery there are only two croissants left. It doesn't matter, I'm, there is only two croissants left It's okay, I'm going to buy those two croissants, it will give me 9 croissants in total, and I still need one I go to the third bakery and I buy one more croissant so I will have paid 14 euros, this is a 40% sleepage compared to the initial 10 euros The initial order value is 10 % sleepage and our initial 10€ so now we see that if my order had gone from 10€ at 0.4%, and of 10% in the slippage my order would never have been executed or I would have needed to wait for a long time I would have needed to wait for the next day for bakery number 1 to be a 10 croissant But maybe the order would have never been executed Let imagine that tomorrow the price of flour increases. So bakery n°1 is going to increase the prices of its croissants so I'll have my order that will be never carried. On the other hand, putting the slippage at 40% allowed me to execute my order, let's say, quite rapidly or at least more quickly because all of a sudden we had a margin of 40% so it went looking at other sellers who were selling a bit more expensive. I hope you understand better this notion of sleepage. The goal is to find the right compromise between speed and value, if you want your wait to be carried out as quickly as possible, you'll have to increase the sleepage but too, but you'll pay you more. So, please find the right compromise. If you're not buying too fast and if you're not in a rush period, you can start starting with a short SLEEPH and start increasing.
